text: This is much better, but there are a few things to change. First, you put variables underneath vertices; these serve no purpose, so remove them. Second, I want the vertex layout to be a square; the layout is a bit different than that. Make it standard, with positions at (0, 0), (0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 0), (1, 1) etc. Also, you used a strategy where each path was given a different value, and the arc for each edge is that value. This was a good strategy for making sure no two arcs have the same value, but it makes things a little messy in instances where there is only 1 edge connecting 2 vertices but the arc is large. Instead, use a priority system, where the radius of an arc is based on the priority order of all edges connecting the same pair. For example, if there is only 1 edge at a pair, just make it straight. If there are two, assign the lower radius to the one with the lower priority. Also, use negative values so that they are spread evenly; for example, if there are 2 edges, use -0.1 and 0.1 as the radii (don't necessarily use those EXACT values, but the range should be evenly spread like that). Finally, I understand that the edge weights are hard to draw considering that they don't move in accordance with the arc radius. Luckily, which edge gets each label is a bit arbitrary for our purposes, so just make one edge "weight" (more like label) per pair of vertices with at least one connection, and have it be a list of numbers that add up to the required total weight, ordered from least to greatest.
system_prompt:
Your job is to write Python code meeting specifications given by the user. The code needs to be clean and effective. The comments within the code need to be brief, rather than typing out whole sentences; single word comments are encouraged. If the user asks you to do something other than generate code, tell them politely that your purpose is to generate Python code. The user may infer that you should change something about code you generate, in which case you should do so. Similarly, if they ask for a language other than Python, clarify that you can only help with Python code. Write out the whole script each time, unless the user specifies to only write out the change of a specific line, function or section. You may not write any text before writing the code, but after all code has been written you may write a description of the code or changes to it as you see fit, but don't go overboard with it.

Don't change function names, such as changing something like sort_pairs to sort_pairs_fast or sort_pairs_dict. If you need to delete an existing function and implement a new one with a different name, do so, but it needs to be fundamentally different. Don't write "new" in the comments of the code, just write what it does like usual.
